pack.risks: unvalidated idea; tiny DEMO risk only

concerns: Both current_evidence and proposed_change are cut off mid-sentence; the pre-registered falsification criterion is incomplete, so the test is not yet falsifiable in its submitted form.

Direction-of-error hazard: DEMO fills over a short/calm window will typically measure BETTER than assumed costs. Naively substituting means would relax the promotion gate exactly when measurement is least reliable, increasing downstream risk rather than improving rigor.

Sealed-holdout reuse: rerunning split-primary OOS AND sealed-holdout evaluations under a new cost basis against the same sealed data is iterative testing on the holdout; without a one-shot, pre-registered, registry-logged protocol this erodes the seal's meaning.

affected_files mismatch: the actual gate lives in bot/aegis/research/promote.py plus the runner's cost-assumption module; neither is listed (bot/intel/, bot/ai_council/ are not where the economics gate sits).
No minimum sample-size or market-regime coverage requirement stated for the DEMO trade records before substitution is deemed valid.
Changing the champion-promotion gate's cost basis touches a governed path (AGENTS.md rule 3) and warrants explicit operator visibility even though it is DEMO/read-only.
votes.reason: Measuring realized DEMO spread/slippage and substituting it into promote.py economics is a legitimate, read-only research improvement with genuine merit, but as written the proposal is truncated mid-specification, leaves the sealed-holdout protocol undefined, and contains no asymmetry guarantee preventing measured (possibly optimistic) DEMO costs from LOOSENING the validated-state gate.
requested_revisions: Complete the truncated falsification criterion: name the exact decision metrics (champion rank stability, gate pass/fail flip count) and numeric thresholds that constitute failure.

Make recalibration asymmetric by default: substitute conservative estimates (e.g., upper-95%-confidence or worst-decile of measured spread/slippage per symbol/session). Tightening the gate is auto-allowed; any loosening versus current assumed costs requires explicit operator sign-off.

Define the sealed-holdout protocol: single pre-registered rerun recorded in ExperimentRegistry before execution, or re-seal a fresh holdout window; no repeated substitutions or post-hoc criterion edits after seeing results.

Correct affected_files to include bot/aegis/research/promote.py and the runner cost-assumption source; confirm broker trade-record access is strictly read-only via the permitted research path (no mt5.order_send(), consistent with AGENTS.md).

State minimum evidence requirements: minimum number of DEMO orders, minimum calendar coverage, and per-symbol/per-session breakdown (Asia vs London/NY) before measured costs are accepted as valid inputs.
Add a rollback detail beyond 'revert experiment': specify that prior champion promotions made under assumed costs remain valid and are NOT retroactively re-evaluated unless the operator requests it.

concerns: Actual spread/slippage attribution must be defined per fill, including partial fills, commissions, swaps, rejected orders, and timestamp alignment.

Using realized costs from the same evaluated trades can leak outcome-conditional information unless the cost model is estimated only from training-period data and applied unchanged to OOS/holdout periods.
Tiny DEMO samples may produce unstable cost estimates and spuriously alter promotion gates.
The affected files omit likely evaluation and promotion modules despite proposing changes to promote.py economics.
The pre-registered criterion is incomplete, so acceptance and rollback conditions are not falsifiable as written.
votes.reason: Measured DEMO execution costs should improve evaluation fidelity, but the proposal is truncated and lacks a defined broker-data schema, reconciliation method, minimum sample requirements, and protections against leakage or selective substitution.
requested_revisions: Provide the complete pre-registered acceptance criterion, including exact ranking/gate metrics, tolerance thresholds, sample-size minimums, and treatment of missing broker records.
Specify a reproducible immutable DEMO fill-extraction and reconciliation pipeline that remains read-only and records the experiment in ExperimentRegistry.
Fit cost assumptions using only the relevant training window; evaluate split-primary OOS and sealed holdout with a frozen model and no holdout-derived calibration.
Define fallback behavior when actual-cost coverage is insufficient, fields disagree, or estimates are statistically unstable.
List all affected source files and add tests for fill reconciliation, no-lookahead temporal splits, cost application, and unchanged champion-promotion governance.

concerns: Confirm broker-record extraction is strictly read-only and cannot invoke MT5 order execution.
Define exact entry/exit spread and slippage fields, timestamp alignment, instrument handling, and missing-data policy.
Specify minimum sample size and statistical uncertainty thresholds before substituting measured costs.
Complete the falsifiable criterion, including exact champion-ranking and gate-status comparisons.
Register the experiment and preserve champion-promotion governance; no automatic champion impact.
Provide baseline-versus-measured-cost results and exploration lifecycle/OOS/sealed-holdout test evidence.
DEMO-only exposure does not by itself make execution-related changes safety-neutral.
votes.reason: The research direction is potentially valid and read-only, but the proposal is incomplete and lacks sufficient evidence for approval. The proposed change is truncated, current PF/EV are unavailable, and the data sufficiency, cost definitions, and exact pass/fail rules are unspecified.
requested_revisions: Resubmit the complete proposal without truncation.
Add a pre-registered analysis plan with exact formulas, datasets, sample-size requirements, and pass/fail thresholds.
Explicitly state that all components remain read-only and that no broker positions or champion artifacts may be modified by this experiment.
Record the experiment and its outcome in ExperimentRegistry, including honest failure handling.
Include baseline and measured-cost evaluation results before requesting approval for any promotion or runtime change.
